# bide-anchor command reference

<!-- Generated by TestReference in cmd/bide-anchor from what the commands print for -h. Do not edit:
     run go test . -run TestReference -update in cmd/bide-anchor. CI fails when this page is stale. -->

bide-anchor verifies and exports the signed tree heads that an object-store anchor wrote to a bucket: `-backend s3` for the S3 Object Lock anchor (`anchor/awss3`), the default, and `-backend gcs` for the Google Cloud Storage anchor (`anchor/gcs`), which takes `-project` (the project number) in place of `-owner`.
It is a separate program in its own module, so that the cloud SDKs of the anchors it reads are not in `bide`:

```sh
go install github.com/bide-ai/bide/cmd/bide-anchor@latest
```

How the anchor works, the bucket and IAM setup, and what each check shows and does not show, are in
[the anchoring guide](../guides/anchoring.md). Flags take one dash, as in `bide`. Credentials come from the cloud
SDK's default chain (the AWS chain, or Application Default Credentials for gcs), never from flags; a server other than AWS is selected with
`AWS_ENDPOINT_URL_S3` and `-path-style`. Exit status is 0 for success, 1 for a head or object that did not verify
or a finding, 2 for a usage error, and 3 when the bucket's state is unknown: an online read was unavailable, denied or timed out, so the audit did not finish. Retry, and alert if it persists; an aborted audit is never a pass and is not a finding.

| Command | What it does |
|---|---|
| [`bide-anchor verify`](#bide-anchor-verify) | offline: check every object in a directory of downloaded anchor objects |
| [`bide-anchor export`](#bide-anchor-export) | write the verified heads of one run or trail, one per line, for `bide audit -heads` |
| [`bide-anchor check`](#bide-anchor-check) | online, read-only: verify the heads and report how they are stored |

## bide-anchor verify

```
Usage of bide-anchor verify:
  -backend string
    	the object store the anchor wrote to: s3, gcs (default "s3")
  -dir string
    	a directory of downloaded anchor objects
  -kind string
    	the tree kind: journal, or events for a notification or event trail (default "journal")
  -pubkey string
    	the log operator's public key (ed25519:<hex>, or a file holding it)
  -run string
    	only this run or trail ID (default: every one)
```

## bide-anchor export

```
Usage of bide-anchor export:
  -backend string
    	the object store the anchor wrote to: s3, gcs (default "s3")
  -bucket string
    	read this anchor bucket (online, with read-only credentials)
  -dir string
    	read a directory of downloaded anchor objects (offline)
  -force
    	with -bucket: export even when the lock audit has findings
  -kind string
    	the tree kind: journal, or events for a notification or event trail (default "journal")
  -kms-key string
    	the KMS key the heads must be encrypted with (gcs: projects/P/locations/L/keyRings/R/cryptoKeys/K; s3: a key ID (UUID), an mrk- key ID or a key ARN, nothing else, not an alias): a bucket default or an object with another key is a finding
  -lock-mode string
    	-backend s3: the object lock mode the anchor was configured with, COMPLIANCE or GOVERNANCE: a bucket default that is weaker is a finding, and with GOVERNANCE a governance-locked object is not
  -o string
    	write to this file instead of standard output
  -owner string
    	-backend s3: the 12-digit AWS account ID that owns the bucket (with -bucket)
  -path-style
    	use path-style addressing (a non-AWS server)
  -prefix string
    	the key prefix the anchor was configured with (default bide-anchor/)
  -project string
    	-backend gcs: the number of the Google Cloud project that owns the bucket (with -bucket)
  -pubkey string
    	the log operator's public key (ed25519:<hex>, or a file holding it)
  -retention duration
    	the retention the anchor was configured with: a bucket retention shorter than this (and, for s3, an object retained for less from its own write) is a finding; without it only the 24 h minimum is checked. A default retention in years counts as 365 days a year (7 years: 2555 days, 61320h), so pass at most that
  -run string
    	the run or trail ID
  -timeout duration
    	with -bucket: give up after this long and exit 3 (state unknown); 0: no limit (default 5m0s)
```

## bide-anchor check

```
Usage of bide-anchor check:
  -backend string
    	the object store the anchor wrote to: s3, gcs (default "s3")
  -bucket string
    	read this anchor bucket (online, with read-only credentials)
  -kind string
    	the tree kind: journal, or events for a notification or event trail (default "journal")
  -kms-key string
    	the KMS key the heads must be encrypted with (gcs: projects/P/locations/L/keyRings/R/cryptoKeys/K; s3: a key ID (UUID), an mrk- key ID or a key ARN, nothing else, not an alias): a bucket default or an object with another key is a finding
  -lock-mode string
    	-backend s3: the object lock mode the anchor was configured with, COMPLIANCE or GOVERNANCE: a bucket default that is weaker is a finding, and with GOVERNANCE a governance-locked object is not
  -owner string
    	-backend s3: the 12-digit AWS account ID that owns the bucket (with -bucket)
  -path-style
    	use path-style addressing (a non-AWS server)
  -prefix string
    	the key prefix the anchor was configured with (default bide-anchor/)
  -project string
    	-backend gcs: the number of the Google Cloud project that owns the bucket (with -bucket)
  -pubkey string
    	the log operator's public key (ed25519:<hex>, or a file holding it)
  -retention duration
    	the retention the anchor was configured with: a bucket retention shorter than this (and, for s3, an object retained for less from its own write) is a finding; without it only the 24 h minimum is checked. A default retention in years counts as 365 days a year (7 years: 2555 days, 61320h), so pass at most that
  -run string
    	the run or trail ID
  -timeout duration
    	with -bucket: give up after this long and exit 3 (state unknown); 0: no limit (default 5m0s)
```
